title: A staggered Lean project to shorten urinary catheter duration on 12 wards in four hospitals
abstract: Problem: urinary catheters stayed longer than needed on 12 wards in four hospitals. Intervention: value stream mapping and standard work (nurse-driven removal, huddle check, removal reminder), introduced one hospital per quarter as the Lean coach moved. Measures: monthly catheter days per 100 patient days (primary), infections (descriptive), indication documentation (process) and reinsertion within 72 hours (balancing). Results will be written after March 2028.
introduction: Catheter duration is driven by handoffs where the indication is lost. Nurse-driven removal reduces catheter days in multi-hospital series, while infection effects are imprecise.
methods: Multiple-baseline interrupted time series with hospital-specific change points and hospital-specific levels; Hospital D used point counts for its whole series. The project was screened as quality improvement.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will show each hospital's series with its start marked, the pooled level change, infections, documentation and reinsertion.
discussion: The discussion will separate the level change at each start from regional trends using the hospitals not yet started. It will report infections descriptively and will not claim an infection effect.
limitations: The order of hospitals was fixed by coach availability, not randomised. Hospital D used a different measurement source, and infections were too few to test.
conclusion: To be written after the final hospital's six-month follow-up. It will state whether catheter days fell at each start and whether reinsertion stayed within its threshold.
summary: SQUIRE draft for the staggered project; results empty until data exist.
